title: Thanksgiving Showdown: NFL Week 12 Highlights Reveal Epic Plays, Surprises & Rivalries on ESPN
body:
The NFL’s Thanksgiving slate delivered a whirlwind of drama, with the Detroit Lions hosting the Chicago Bears in the opening contest, the Dallas Cowboys facing the New York Giants in the afternoon showdown, and the Buffalo Bills taking on the Miami Dolphins in the primetime slot. Each game produced its own share of game‑changing moments, from clutch fourth‑quarter scores to defensive heroics that reshaped the early‑season narratives for several clubs. By the night’s end, the Lions secured a hard‑earned victory, the Cowboys emerged victorious in a tightly contested battle, and the Bills clinched a dramatic win that kept their playoff aspirations alive.

The Lions‑Bears encounter began as a classic rivalry, with Detroit’s offense finally finding rhythm after a sluggish start. Quarterback Jared Goff, who had struggled to generate momentum in his first five starts, connected on a 45‑yard strike to Amon-Ra St. Brown early in the second quarter, setting up the Lions’ first touchdown. Detroit’s ground game, anchored by D’Andre Swift, added a 12‑yard rush that capped a 14‑7 lead at halftime. Chicago responded late in the third quarter with a 32‑yard touchdown pass from Justin Fields to D.J. Moore, narrowing the margin to 14‑13. However, a decisive defensive stand by the Lions in the fourth quarter—highlighted by a strip‑sack from Aidan Hutchinson that resulted in a turnover—allowed Goff to find rookie tight end Sam LaPorta for a go‑ahead score. The Bears’ final drive stalled at the Lions’ 22‑yard line, sealing Detroit’s 21‑13 triumph and ending a three‑year Thanksgiving losing streak.

The afternoon matchup between the Cowboys and Giants lived up to its billing as a pivotal NFC East duel. Dallas entered the game with a 4‑2 record, while New York, 3‑3, hoped to stay within striking distance of the division lead. Early on, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott orchestrated a methodical drive that culminated in a 7‑yard touchdown pass to wide‑out CeeDee Lamb, establishing a 7‑0 lead. The Giants answered with a balanced attack, leveraging Daniel Jones’s dual‑threat ability; a 15‑yard scramble set up a 23‑yard field goal, and later a 4th‑and‑2 conversion led to a 9‑yard touchdown run by Saquon Barkley, flipping the score to 14‑10 in New York’s favor at halftime.

The second half turned into a defensive chess match. Dallas’s pass rush, led by Micah Parsons, applied relentless pressure, forcing two sacks and a forced fumble that the Cowboys recovered deep in Giants territory. Prescott capitalized with a 22‑yard strike to Michael Gallup, extending the lead to 21‑10. New York rallied with a 48‑yard field goal, narrowing the gap to three points. With just over two minutes left, the Giants drove into Cowboys territory, but a crucial interception by safety Trevon Diggs halted the comeback. The Cowboys secured a 21‑13 victory, bolstering their position atop the NFC East and giving head coach Mike McCarthy a much‑needed win against a familiar foe.

In the primetime slot, the Bills faced a resilient Dolphins squad that had surprised many with a 6‑0 start to the season. Buffalo’s offense, led by quarterback Josh Allen, appeared sluggish early, managing only a field goal in the first quarter. Miami, however, capitalized on a turnover, with quarterback Tua Tagovailoa connecting with tight end Hunter Henry for a 31‑yard touchdown, taking a 7‑3 lead into halftime. The second half saw a dramatic shift. Allen, after a brief period of indecision, unleashed a 44‑yard pass to wide‑out Gabe Davis, setting up a 5‑yard rushing touchdown by Devin Singletary that tied the game. The decisive moment arrived with 1:12 remaining when Allen, under pressure, scrambled and launched a 28‑yard touchdown pass to wide‑out Marquez Valdes‑Scantling, putting Buffalo ahead 17‑14. The Dolphins’ final possession ended with a sack by Bills linebacker Matt Milano, sealing the win.

Beyond the scores, the Thanksgiving games offered a microcosm of the league’s evolving storylines. Detroit’s victory reaffirms the Lions’ resurgence under head coach Dan Campbell, suggesting they may finally shed the “perennial underdog” label.
